title: Who's Who: Léonie Marchand
summary: Aperture physicist whose work remains part of the record of modern Eidetics.
author: Who's Who Desk
paragraphs: The Correspondent adds Léonie Marchand (1787–1859) to its Who's Who of Eideticians, recording a aperture physicist whose name still attends serious discussion of the Eidetic Stratum.

Marchand separated a common diffraction spot from the rare conditions that create an Eidetic aperture. In 1822 she established thresholds of alignment, surface finish, and concordance, giving laboratories a practical test for extravagant claims.
She declined to name an opening after herself, preferring the apparatus to be copied.

For Alderwick readers, Léonie Marchand is remembered not as an ornament to legend but as a figure whose work helps explain why Eideticians prize careful terms, repeatable evidence and a sober account of what remains unknown.
